newsitem.title: CANADA: ALPINE SKIING-MEN'S WORLD CUP SUPER G CANCELED.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-MEN'S WORLD CUP SUPER G CANCELED.

text.p: The season's opening World Cup Alpine skiing men's super giant slalom was cancelled on Sunday due to heavy overnight snowfall and poor visibility at Whistler Mountain.
The announcement was made at noon EST (1700 GMT) by the race organising committee and International Ski Federation (FIS) officials.

Upwards of seven inches (20 cm) fell overnight, adding to the already extensive snowfall which had wiped out Saturday's men's downhill and the three training runs earlier in the week in preparation for the season opening men's speed races.
There was some irony that excessive snowfall forced the cancellation after officials had made a great deal of man-made snow in preparation for the racing.
A total of 633 course workers spent over 30,000 man hours, many in darkness, preparing the course.
The men's and women's Alpine Ski World Cup circuit now moves to Val d'Isere, France, for men's and women's downhill and super giant slalom races this week.
